## QUESTION 1

1. __Repeat the classification exercise using 2 different algorithms/models. Explain the differences between the 3 models__ (your original one, and the 2 new ones for this task).

_My original model was a random forest classifier. That one had an 80% accuracy overall. My two new models were SGDClassifier, and NearestCentroid. I can immediately see that SGD is focused on gathering as many possibilites as it can, since it has a recall of 100% at the precision's expense. It's only 61% accurate. The NearestCentroid model favors precision a little over recall, which boosts its f1-score and accuracy. Although, neither of these models seem as trustworthy as the random forest classifier._

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here

feature = df.select("netprice", "livearea", "stories")
target = df.select("before1980")
x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(feature, target, test_size=0.1, random_state=20)
print(x_train.shape, y_train.shape)
print(x_test.shape, y_test.shape)
sgd = SGDClassifier()
sgd.fit(x_train, y_train)
sgd_pred = sgd.predict(x_test)
print(classification_report(y_test, sgd_pred))

nc = NearestCentroid()
nc.fit(x_train, y_train)
nc_pred = nc.predict(x_test)
print(classification_report(y_test, nc_pred))
```


## QUESTION 2

1. For each model (your original one, and the 2 new ones for this task), display the classification report and the permutation importances for the most important features.  Discuss which model you would recommend to the Client and why.

_I would still recommend using the RandomForestClassifier. It beats the other two models in accuracy by at least 10%, and it does not pull every bit of data it can (including negative results). When making decisions, the RandomForestClassifier factors in all of its features (where each feature has a 10 - 13% influence). The other two models don't use all of their features to make a choice, which is what those zeroes mean._

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
rf_classifier = RandomForestClassifier()
rf_classifier.fit(x_train, y_train)
rf_pred = rf_classifier.predict(x_test)

# original
result = permutation_importance(rf_classifier, x_test, y_test, n_repeats = 10, random_state = 42)
perms_imp = pl.DataFrame({'importance': result.importances_mean, 'vars': x_train.columns})
print("Original")
print(perms_imp.sort(['importance'], descending= True))

# SGD
result = permutation_importance(sgd, x_test, y_test, n_repeats = 10, random_state = 42)
perms_imp = pl.DataFrame({'importance': result.importances_mean, 'vars': x_train.columns})
print("SGDClassifier")
print(perms_imp.sort(['importance'], descending= True))

# NearestCentroid
result = permutation_importance(nc, x_test, y_test, n_repeats = 10, random_state = 42)
perms_imp = pl.DataFrame({'importance': result.importances_mean, 'vars': x_train.columns})
print("NearestCentroid")
print(perms_imp.sort(['importance'], descending= True))

```
